cs.label: [section] Cíl předmětu a studijní výstupy:
cs.content: Course Description This course will enable students to understand the function of root systems and their mycorrhizal symbionts and identify the anatomical, morphological, and physiological parameters of roots and their distribution in space and time that underlie resource uptake. Students will learn about root and mycorrhizal classification (both morphotypes and DNA), morphological analysis, and their functional biodiversity. Practical sessions will include sampling and identifying mycorrhizal morphotypes, studying interactions of mycorrhizal fungi with roots, and exploring the effects of ontogeny, competitors etc. on root system plasticity and mycorrhiza diversity/identity. Course Objectives By the end of this course, students can: • Understand the function and structure of root systems. • Identify anatomical, morphological, and physiological parameters of roots. • Classify roots and perform morphological analysis. • Understand the biodiversity and function of mycorrhizae. • Identify mycorrhizal morphotypes and understand their interactions with roots and soil biota. • Explore the effects of key biotic and abiotic factors on root systems and soil fungal communities. Skills Acquired • Identification of key anatomical, morphological, and physiological parameters of roots • Sampling and classification of roots • Sampling and identifying mycorrhizal morphotypes • Basic understanding of soil, root and EM sampling and processing for genetic analyses of the fungal community • Understanding root-mycorrhizal interactions and their ecological roles • Analysis of abiotic effects on root systems and soil fungal communities • Application of recent scientific developments in the field of root and mycorrhizal ecology to forest ecosystem studies
